core_obligations: Quote the equivalence of (1) and (2) from the preceding lemma of the same section and the equivalence of (4) and (5) from the cited Algebra lemma, and note that (3) and (5) are equivalent by definition (proof lines 4896-4901).

Use that a localisation of a torsion free module is torsion free to show that (1) implies (5), since a module with no associated prime other than the zero ideal is exactly one with no embedded associated prime (proof lines 4902-4905).

Assume (5) and suppose M has a torsion element; then M contains an embedding of R/I for a nonzero ideal I, which gives an associated prime different from the zero ideal and embedded, contradicting the assumption (proof lines 4905-4910).

difficulty_reason: The lemma collects five equivalent conditions for a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian domain: torsion freeness, being a submodule of a finite free module, having no associated prime other than the zero ideal, having the zero ideal in its support together with property (S_1), and having the zero ideal in its support with no embedded associated prime (statement lines 4883-4893). The proof is a 16-line web of implications (proof lines 4896-4911) which routes through the localisation lemma already proved in the section and through the theory of associated primes: (1) is equivalent to (2) by the preceding statement, (4) is equivalent to (5) by a lemma of the Algebra chapter, (3) is equivalent to (5) immediately from the definition, then localisation of a torsion free module is used to show (1) implies (5), and finally the reverse implication finds, under the negation of (5), an embedding of R/I for a nonzero ideal I into M and hence an embedded associated prime. The step that a reader has to follow is the last one, where a torsion element is converted into an associated prime of M and the embeddedness of that prime is what contradicts (5).
